title: Help me get to where you guys are
author: tfy-cape-town
selftext:
I need to level up.

Currently im using claude code cli. Running the godot mcp.

I create a new project in godot. I start claude code cli instance in the new godot folder. After some fiddling I get godot mcp running. I do /remote-control so I can manage it from claude.ai

I am aware of the blender mcp and will be using that shortly. But claude graphics is pretty crappy.

I read somewhere of using nanogpt skill for gfx.

I am unfamiliar with workflows and skills. Done some reading but struggling wrapping my head around the applications etc for game development.

Have done about 5 crappy games so far just to experiment and play around.

But some good solid foundations from you guys would be helpful to take it to the next level.

replies.author: geddy
replies.body:
Fable is one of Claude’s agents. Run /model in the CLI and you can pick which model to use, along with the effort. 

I recommend against using Fable right away.. it’ll chew through tokens like they’re nothing. Heck I run Sonnet on medium and it’s been doing great, keep myself under the limit. 

Another pro tip is if you have any repeated things you need to do, rather than asking the bot each time and burning tokens, have it create a script to do it and then just use the script directly. 

For instance for deployments I used to have Claude do it, before I realized that was silly and I could just set up a script and run it myself with two commands to kick my work up to prod.

replies.author: tfy-cape-town
replies.body: Yeah, did figure it out. Uses too much tokens. Opus and sonnet has been great.

comments.author: derAres
comments.body:
Maps/levels: provise a birds eye view layout and tell it to build the geometry / shape first, then iterate.

Decoration: habe ai place it for you, but you will do a lot of rearranging manually

Texture: use open source libraries and have it procedurally generate em for you

Animations: use stuff from mixamo and have it build you a simple animation studio to add your unique animations if you need more

Models: simple furniture-level stuff: astra is great at it. For more complex stuff use a service like tripo

3d chars: tripo / meshy

And what i learned to be of vital importance: have ai build you tools to help you prompt it more easily, for example a report function ingame where you point at something and hit R and type „scale bigger by factor 2“.

replies.author: tfy-cape-town
replies.body: Cool thanks. Specifically I want to know about useful skills and workflows. Some posts, authors have numerous ai's working together with an orchestrator. I have just been working with one instance of the cli.

replies.author: Jameshardy1988
replies.body: You mention an animation studio. What do you mean by this and how would it work? I'm currently building a game with 3D models in it and need some more unique poses that I can't source online, so this will be really useful info for me.

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: Basically have claude build you a tool where you manually move the limbs of your char by dragging them around. The create snaphots on a timeline (animation duration). Then a „export to game“ function. Claude will be able to tell you more.

comments.author: Sharp-Physics-2925
comments.body:
Always start without a blockout. then work with opus 5.5 on medium+ in blender mcp to build out your custom models.

dont expect a 1 shot prompt for a perfect model. You needto work with it and select which pieces are refined.

Dont have it refine the whole model all at once. do specific parts per prompt.  

But also dont expect Triple AAA game quality models.  you can get decent low-poly to mid-poly indie game models

comments.author: Odd-Bench6264
comments.body:
A few tips from another artistically challenged programmer:

If your scene looks shitty, give ChatGPT a screenshot and ask it to reimagine it with better graphics. Be specific about the style: it should look like an in-game screenshot made of sprites or 3D models, not concept art. You probably won’t recreate it perfectly, but it gives you something concrete to aim for. GPT-image-2 and 2.5 are really something else - for me these models have been game changers.

For 3D characters, iterate on concepts with ChatGPT. Stick mostly to humanoids, avoid loose clothing, and use neutral, symmetrical poses. Generate weapons and equipment separately. Turn the images into models with Tripo or Meshy, then use Mixamo for rigging and animations.

Give those assets to Opus 5.5 or Astra with headless Blender—no MCP needed. Ask it to attach weapons, combine or tweak animations, and fix specific mesh, rig, or texture issues. I’ve been amazed at what Opus 5.5 can salvage from badly meshed, poorly rigged assets and a handful of Mixamo animations.

Paseo or Conductor helps you manage multiple Claude Code/Codex agents in isolated worktrees. Have your agents build **debug scenes** so you can easily test what they implement.

For games that suit a rule-based player bot—especially those needing only one action every few seconds—have your agents build one. It gives them a way to simulate matches, test their changes, and iterate on balance.
